hints: Look carefully at where each letter sits on the curves. P is on the rising slope of the temperature graph, Q is at the peak, and S is still just above the baseline on the pH graph.
Remember what makes rate rise with temperature (more collisions and successful enzyme-substrate complexes) versus what makes it fall (disruption of bonds and change in active site shape).
walkthrough:
**Read what each point really means**

Look at the left graph first. P is on the way up, so rate is increasing. Q is at the top, so this is the optimum temperature.

On the right graph, R is at the top, so this is the optimum pH. S is low down on the far right, so rate is very low but not quite zero.

**Link the shape to the molecules**

As temperature rises toward the optimum, enzyme and substrate gain kinetic energy. They collide more often and form more enzyme-substrate complexes.

That complex is held together temporarily by weak interactions such as hydrogen bonds between active site and substrate.

**Test each statement against the points**

At P the enzyme is working well and forming complexes, so A fits. At Q kinetic energy is high but it keeps rising if you heat further, so B is wrong.

At R the enzyme is at its best, so bonds are not breaking. At S there is still a little activity, so it cannot be completely denatured.

options.A: Correct. At P the enzyme is active and rate is rising as more enzyme-substrate complexes form, held by temporary hydrogen bonds.
options.B: False. Kinetic energy increases continuously with temperature, so it is even higher to the right of Q where rate falls due to denaturation.
options.C: False. R is the optimum pH with maximum rate, so the active site is intact and bonds are not breaking there.
options.D: False. At S the curve is still above zero, so some activity remains and the enzyme is not completely denatured.
